content_of_post_to_comment: No, many people did not prefer "the factory" over "the farm.” They preferred the factory's **wages** and then-urban-only **amenities** like electricity and plumbing. People don't leave the countryside for the coal mines and slaughterhouses because they "want" to. Of course, many people did prefer urban life to farming, as ~90% of us were farmers in 1600, and no activity, outside of Maslow's basic hierarchy of needs, is enjoyed by ~90% of people. Even now in modern "late-stage capitalism" America, ~30% of households garden for food, ~10% keep chickens, and ~2% keep other farm animals. Say the "AI utopia" scenario occurs: do you think those numbers go up or down if people had more free time? Despite what you hear on this app, a significant portion of humanity yearns to steward the land. Not everyone, of course. But farming the countryside has been an idyllic goal for humans for **millennia.**
comment: The deeper question may be whether automation changes our relationship with land. Farming could shift from economic necessity back toward craft, stewardship, and identity—but access to land may become the real constraint.
